label: Cycle 1 — Baseline
notes:
First Lingo CGM wear (sensor 1). May 28–29 had the worst hypo cluster of the period — nadir 55 mg/dL for 100 minutes on May 29 midday, and sustained low from May 28 23:44 through May 29 early AM. All morning spikes were post-breakfast (7–10am window), with Jun 1 being the highest single reading at 166. May 30 was a perfect 100% TIR day — that day's meals are the baseline template. No dawn phenomenon detected: overnight glucose naturally declines through 3–6am on most nights. Jun 4 overnight nadir of 55 occurred during sleep.

NO ACV used at any meal during this entire cycle. All spike and hypo data reflects a pure baseline diet with no ACV intervention. This makes Cycle 1 the definitive ACV-absent control that all future cycles with ACV can be compared against.

LOGGING CONVENTION: All meal timestamps in the daily log represent first bite time, matching the CGM onset lag window (typically 30–45 min after first bite for carbohydrate-driven spikes).
